title: Frontend: Counter Using React
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Counter Using React. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({initial=0}). A counter clamped to 0..5 has Increment, Decrement and Reset buttons. Render count in [data-testid="count"]. Disable unavailable increment/decrement, and reset to initial (initial is valid).
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Represent the count in one state value and use functional updaters when the next value depends on the previous one.
alternativeApproaches: Support a changed step size without allowing updates to escape the valid range.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Lower/upper limits; reset; rapid activation.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
